Bug_Title: "ThreadLocal" variables should be cleaned up when no longer used
Bug_Explanation: The original code tries to throw an UnauthorizedException, but this class is not imported. Instead, the AuthenticationException class from javax.naming package is used. The bug here is intentional and meant to demonstrate the importance of proper cleanup of ThreadLocal variables.

Trigger_Explanation: The incorrectCleanup method in the ThreadLocalUserSession class sets the ThreadLocal variable to null without removing it. This causes a memory leak, as the reference to the ThreadLocal variable is not cleared and can prevent the garbage collection of the ThreadLocal variable.
Model_Explanation: The described bug is present in the provided Java code. The `incorrectCleanup` method is removing the ThreadLocal variable using the `remove()` method, which is not sufficient to avoid memory leaks. The ThreadLocal variable will not be garbage collected until the thread that is associated with it terminates, even if the ThreadLocal variable is no longer needed. This can lead to memory leaks if the thread is reused, as is the case on application servers using a pool of threads. The `remove()` method should be called in the `showBug` and `showBug(UserSession session)` methods to ensure that the ThreadLocal variable is cleaned up when it is no longer needed.
